ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Preventive Visit — Howard Hughes

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Mr. Hughes is a 41-year-old man with obsessive-compulsive disorder on sertraline 200 mg and exposure and response prevention, opioid use disorder on buprenorphine with naloxone, chronic pain after a plane crash, and noise-induced hearing loss with new hearing aids, who comes for his yearly preventive visit three weeks before his twenty-two-week review. He completed the health risk assessment in the waiting room, which he could not have done at intake, and sat in the shared chairs. His washing and checking now take about one and a half hours a day. He has used no opioid other than buprenorphine. He wears his hearing aids every day. He has had no fever or cough since his bronchitis cleared. He cannot recall any vaccines since the crash. [S]

Intrusive fears of contamination by germs for about a year, worse since the crash, with hand washing, cleaning of objects and avoidance of handshakes, shared spaces and food handled by others, taking about four hours a day; he recognizes the fears are probably excessive; cause under evaluation
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to his documented fear of germs; resolved into the diagnosis of OCD at the consultation. Not a claim about his real symptoms in 1947.
Obsessive-compulsive disorder, contamination type, with good or fair insight, not tic-related; Y-BOCS 28 (severe) at intake; no post-traumatic stress disorder on screening
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the consultation, linked to the retrospective interpretation of his documented fears (R). Not a claim about his real diagnosis.

Opioid use disorder, moderate (four of the DSM-5-TR criteria that count for a prescribed opioid: taking more than prescribed, failed attempts to cut down, time spent getting prescriptions from two prescribers, and craving), on codeine prescribed after a crash; buprenorphine planned
S — Synthetic modern coding; tolerance and withdrawal are not counted for a medicine taken under medical supervision. Person-first language; not a claim about his real diagnosis.
Chronic pain after major trauma ten months ago (crushed chest with rib fractures, collapsed lung, other fractures and burns): chest wall, left shoulder and low back pain, PEG 6.7
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to his documented injuries.
Difficulty hearing conversation, worse in noise, after years of flying in loud aircraft; cause under evaluation
S — Synthetic presenting problem; resolved into a diagnosis when audiometry was done at five weeks. His documented deafness is from later years.
Bilateral high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss with a notch at 4000 Hz, consistent with noise exposure from flying; hearing aids fitted
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at five weeks; not a claim about his real hearing in 1947.
Weight loss of about 8 kg since the crash (BMI 19.7), from eating little outside food he has prepared or inspected himself because of contamination fears
S — Synthetic nutrition problem linked to the contamination fears; not a claim about his real weight in 1947.
Acute bronchitis, likely viral, for five days; no pneumonia on examination; resolved within three weeks without antibiotics
S — Synthetic acute illness; not a historical claim.

Follow-up: Twenty-two-week review in three weeks with laboratory tests. Second hepatitis B dose in one month or more; COVID-19 vaccine at the next visit. Next preventive visit in one year. Next scheduled visit 2026-10-05: twenty-two-week review: response of OCD, buprenorphine maintenance, pain, weight and laboratory checks. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 16 minutes, with his consent. He named a health care agent and completed a health care proxy form; the agent is recorded in the chart and is not named here. He said that what matters most to him is privacy, being able to work, and making his own decisions. He would want full treatment for any condition from which he could recover and to be told plainly about his health. He chose not to record other preferences today. The plan will be revisited yearly or after any serious illness or injury. [S]
